A linear pair is a pair of adjacent angles formed when two lines intersect. The angles shown above form a linear pair.

Content:
The linear pair postulate states the following:

Content:
> If two angles form a linear pair, then they are supplementary.

Content:
The converse is not true. That is, if two angles are supplementary, they do not necessarily form a linear pair.

Content:
To see why, consider the diagram shown below:

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/690283fc338c98fc275550b19e00d5ce]

Content:
Although the angles are supplementary (the sum of their measures is [MATH: 120^\circ + 60^\circ = 180^\circ]), they do not form a linear pair of angles since they are not adjacent.

sections.normalized_html: Given that [MATH: \overline{AD}] is a segment, what is the measure of [MATH: \angle FOD?]
sections.readable_text:
[IMG: /graphics/220698f9973865a966472aeec9b224b1]

Given that [MATH: \overline{AD}] is a segment, what is the measure of [MATH: \angle FOD?]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
Two angles are supplementary if their measures add up to [MATH: 180^\circ,] a straight angle.

Since [MATH: \overline{AD}] is a segment, we have that [MATH: \angle AOF] and [MATH: \angle FOD] are supplementary. [MATH: m \angle AOF + m \angle FOD = 180^\circ]

Therefore, the measure of [MATH: \angle FOD] is given by [MATH: m∠FOD|= 180^{∘} − m∠AOF; = 180^{∘} − 45^{∘}; = 135^{∘}]

sections.normalized_html: Find the measure of an angle that's supplementary to an angle of [MATH: (7x -63)^\circ.]
sections.readable_text: Find the measure of an angle that's supplementary to an angle of [MATH: (7x -63)^\circ.]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
Two angles are supplementary if their measures add up to [MATH: 180^\circ.]

So, the measure of an angle that's supplementary to an angle of [MATH: (7x -63)^\circ] must be

[MATH: 180^{∘} − (7x − 63)^{∘}|= (180 − 7x + 63)^{∘}; = (180 + 63 − 7x)^{∘}; = (243 − 7x)^{∘}.]
